unlisted_practices: Use AI-based computer vision to detect and blur sensitive objects (people, text, screens) in wearable camera video before any person views the raw footage.
Keep a human in the loop to manually verify partially obfuscated video frames when needed to confirm environmental context.
Evaluate anonymization models by manual review of how many sensitive data points are fully obscured rather than relying on mAP50 alone.
Use a multidisciplinary approach to ensure privacy-preserving AI development is fit-for-purpose and robust.
Delete raw video after AI anonymization and remove audio data upon download.
Extend anonymization models with a sensitivity category covering locations such as bathrooms, religious settings, and playgrounds, trained on home and community data.
Choose unobtrusive, ergonomic wearable camera devices such as camera glasses to reduce stigma, discomfort, and injury risk.
Let patients remove wearable cameras whenever they deem it necessary to protect bystander and personal privacy.

screen.reason: This is a perspective piece proposing a privacy-preserving framework using computer vision to blur sensitive video data for remote fall risk monitoring, mentioning an exemplar proof-of-concept rather than reporting a formal empirical study.
